name: Al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur
bio: Al-Aswad belonged to Nahshal of Tamim and lived in Iraq, where he was a companion of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, king of al-Hira. He lost his sight in old age and was known as the dim-sighted poet of Nahshal. His best-known ode, preserved by al-Mufaddal, remembers the tracks he rode to hunt when he could still see. Al-Zirikli places his death around 600 CE.
